overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its October Fresh Fridays program featuring an interview with esthetician Terri Ann Gavin and a live performance by the Lihi Haruvi Trio. Host Terry Carter also shared community updates, elder programming details, and upcoming autumn events.

items.title: Welcome and Opening Remarks
items.summary: Terry Carter welcomed attendees and viewers to the monthly Fresh Fridays program and reflected on summer activities at the center.

items.title: Poetry Reading: "Bobby Doesn't Live Here"
items.summary: Carter recited his poem "Bobby Doesn't Live Here," exploring contemporary Eurocentric beauty ideals and body image.

items.title: Discussion with Terri Ann Gavin
items.summary: Esthetician and SBT Aesthetics founder Terri Ann Gavin discussed Medford's history of Black beauty culture, specialized skincare treatments for conditions like melasma and acne, professional licensing, and entrepreneurial challenges.

items.title: WMCC Elder Services and Donation Announcements
items.summary: Carter highlighted weekly senior lunches served Tuesday through Thursday and encouraged community donations and memberships to support center operations.

items.title: Musical Performance: Lihi Haruvi Trio
items.summary: Saxophonist Lihi Haruvi Means, accompanied by substitute bassist Ehud Ettun and drummer Shirazette Tinnin, performed a set of original compositions and jazz standards.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Upcoming Community Events
items.summary: Carter closed the broadcast by announcing upcoming events, including an on-site flu and COVID-19 vaccine clinic, Senior Club gatherings, a senior spotlight, and the Black Vendor Fair.
